title: Decode a Nested String

concept.title: A stack remembers what to come back to
body: The encoding `k[text]` means that `text` is repeated `k` times, and `text` may itself contain such parts: `3[a2[c]]` is `accaccacc`. When you meet `[`, you start working on an **inner** part, but you must later come back to the **outer** part exactly where you left it. That is a stack.

Keep the current text `cur` and the number `num` that you have read last. On `[`: **push** the pair `(cur, num)` on the stack and start fresh (`cur = ""`, `num = 0`). On `]`: **pop** the saved pair `(prev, k)` and set `cur = prev + cur * k`. A digit extends `num`; a letter extends `cur`.
Numbers can have several digits (`12[a]`), which is why `num` is built with `num * 10 + digit`.

statement: An encoded word follows the rule `k[text]`: the text inside the brackets is repeated `k` times (`k` is a positive number, which may have several digits). The text inside may contain other encoded parts. Letters outside brackets are copied as they are. Print the decoded word.
inputFormat: A single word with lowercase letters, digits and the brackets `[` and `]`. It is valid, and a number always stands directly before a `[`.
constraints: The decoded word has at most 50000 letters.

examples.note: 2[c] is cc, so a2[c] is acc, and three times is accaccacc.

hints: Use a stack of pairs (text so far, repeat count).
On `[` save the current text and the number, then start a new text.
On `]` take the saved pair and set `cur = saved_text + cur * count`.

explanation: The stack stores the text and the repeat count of the outer levels. A closing bracket combines the saved text with the repeated inner text.
solution.complexity: Time O(length of the decoded word), space O(length).

code.python:
s = input().strip()

stack = []
cur = ""
num = 0
for ch in s:
    if "0" <= ch <= "9":
        num = num * 10 + int(ch)
    elif ch == "[":
        stack.append((cur, num))
        cur = ""
        num = 0
    elif ch == "]":
        prev, k = stack.pop()
        cur = prev + cur * k
    else:
        cur += ch
print(cur)
